Hi Dan — great to hear from you and glad the demo resonated. Below is a concise two-option pilot we typically run, with explicit batching/caching/quant guidance and an initial Econ proposal. I attached a compact pricing options PDF and our quant test summary for reference.

Option A — Cache-first pilot (recommended if 70%+ prefix reuse):
- Technical approach: enable prefix KV-cache + conservative batching (max batch window 25ms) to keep tail latency <150ms P95.
- Quantization: int8 for LLM serving; enable per-layer calibration (no int4 in pilot by default). Int8 gives ~1.6–2.2x perf improvement vs fp16 with negligible quality delta.
- Commercial: 30% credit on first 10M tokens/month for 60 days, then 15% on billed usage for next 30 days. Ops: standard pilot support + dedicated response channel; we can commit to 4hr business-hours response and a one-week remediation SLA for regressions if we agree on monitored evals.
- When to pick: workloads with many repeated prompts / system messages where cache hits dominate.

Option B — Throughput-first pilot (recommended for high-concurrency inference):
- Technical approach: aggressive batching (batch window up to 50ms, dynamic batch sizing) and CPU fallback lanes for short requests. KV-cache optional.
- Quantization: int8 baseline; controlled int4 experiment on isolated model snapshot with evaluation harness. Int4 may give 3–4x token throughput but risks small classification/regression deltas — we recommend a guarded rollout (A/B with 5% traffic to start).
- Commercial: 20% credit on first 20M tokens/month for 60 days, plus a one-time $10k usage credit to offset benchmarking. Ops: 24/7 pager for critical incidents (escalation path documented).
- When to pick: high QPS, many short requests, throughput-sensitive SLAs.

Pilot ops & evaluation
- We will run a pre-flight eval (you supply 2–3 representative prompt sets). We’ll run int8 and int4 comparison with automated metric diffing (ROUGE/accuracy + custom business metrics).
- Expected timeline: kickoff week 0, bench/validate week 1–2, pilot week 3–10, review week 11.

Commercial ask / negotiation framing
- For a 50M tokens/month POC: recommend starting with Option A if you expect reuse; we can extend to Option B after validation.
- Concession proposal: 30% credits on first 10M + $10k benchmark credit (Option A) or 20% credits on first 20M + $10k (Option B).
- If EdgeFin commits to a 6-month post-pilot reserved band (commit >= $T/month), we can convert credits into tiered committed discounts (10–25% depending on band).

Next steps
- I attached: Optimize_Toolkit_Pricing_Options_v2.pdf (short, line-itemed) and Quantization_Test_Results.xlsx (sample lab runs).
- Can we schedule a 45-minute workshop with your infra and procurement tomorrow? I’m available 2–4pm PT (booking: https://cal.com/stephanie/edgefin-workshop).

On a couple of operational points: Lauren, can you confirm the escalation path and whether we can stand up the dedicated response channel for this pilot?

Thanks — happy to tighten numbers after a short workshop.

Stephanie — quick technical notes / redlines:

1) Int4 guidance
- I’m comfortable with an int4 experiment but it must be on a non-critical model snapshot behind A/B. Start at 5% traffic and hold for a rolling 7-day eval comparing business metrics (we should capture exact KPIs from EdgeFin). If regressions exceed thresholds we auto-rollback.

2) Eval gating
- Require EdgeFin to provide labeled eval sets for the class of queries they care about (we need at least 2k prompts representative of production to have meaningful signal).

3) Ops / SLA
- Can support 24/7 critical pager for Option B but we need a runbook and a severity matrix signed off. For Option A, 4hr BH response + one-week remediation SLA is OK provided remediation scope excludes third-party infra failures.

4) Caps / financial guardrails
- Approve the proposed credits but add a cap: credits applied up to 30M tokens during pilot. Any overage billed at list rates unless we convert to committed discount. Also request a soft clawback if usage patterns are intentionally inflated (we’ll detect anomalous token spikes).

5) Attachments & follow-up
- I’ll add a short note to the pricing sheet about int4 experimental constraints and update Quantization_Test_Results.xlsx with the sample delta plots.

If Lauren is good on the conversion mechanics, I’m fine with Stephanie locking this into the workshop.
